policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere וַיּוֹחֶל and ketiv וייחל are spelling/stem variants of the same verb (יחל, wait); ASV 'And he tarried' renders either identically, with no italic supply and no note on the verse. Base qere fallback retained.

Qere אָמְרוּ (plural) and ketiv אמר (singular, collective with 'the Philistines') differ only in verb number; ASV 'the Philistines said' does not mark number on the English verb, has no italic supply, and no note on the verse. Base qere fallback retained.
